sanskrit: ataś cāṣṭaguṇaṃ pārtha prāpsyase dharmam uttamam netā ca tvam ṛṣīn yasmāt tena te 'ṣṭaguṇaṃ phalam
english: And beyond this, O Pārtha, you shall attain supreme merit eightfold; since you are the guide of the sages, therefore shall the fruit be eightfold for you.

sanskrit: rakṣogaṇāvakīrṇāni tīrthāny etāni bhārata na gatir vidyate 'nyasya tvām ṛte kurunandana
english: These sacred tirthas, O Bhārata, are overrun by bands of rakshasas — there is no passage for any other, O joy of the Kuru line, save for you.

sanskrit: idaṃ devarṣicaritaṃ sarvatīrthārthasaṃśritam yaḥ paṭhet kalyam utthāya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Whoever rises at dawn and recites this account of the divine sages, which comprises the essence of all the tirthas, shall be freed from all sins.

sanskrit: ṛṣimukhyāḥ sadā yatra vālmīkis tv atha kāśyapaḥ ātreyas tv atha kauṇḍinyo viśvāmitro 'tha gautamaḥ
english: The foremost of sages are ever present there — Vālmīki and Kaśyapa, Ātreya and Kaundinyа, Viśvāmitra and Gautama,

sanskrit: asito devalaś caiva mārkaṇḍeyo 'tha gālavaḥ bharadvājo vasiṣṭhaś ca munir uddālakas tathā
english: And Asita Devala, and Mārkaṇḍeya, and Gālava, and Bharadvāja, and Vasiṣṭha, and the sage Uddālaka as well,

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ saha putreṇa vyāsaś ca japatāṃ varaḥ durvāsāś ca muniśreṣṭho gālavaś ca mahātapāḥ
english: And Śaunaka together with his son, and Vyāsa the foremost among those who recite prayers, and Durvāsā the best of sages, and Gālava of great austerities —

sanskrit: ete ṛṣivarāḥ sarve tvatpratīkṣās tapodhanāḥ ebhiḥ saha mahārāja tīrthāny etāny anuvraja
english: All these greatest of sages, rich in austerities, await you. With them, O great king, do traverse these sacred tirthas.

sanskrit: eṣa vai lomaśo nāma devarṣir amitadyutiḥ sameṣyati tvayā caiva tena sārdham anuvraja
english: And this divine sage named Lomaśa, of boundless radiance, shall join you — travel together with him as well.

sanskrit: mayā ca saha dharmajña tīrthāny etāny anuvraja prāpsyase mahatīṃ kīrtiṃ yathā rājā mahābhiṣaḥ
english: And together with me, O knower of dharma, traverse these tirthas; you shall attain great renown, even as did King Mahābhiṣa.

sanskrit: yathā yayātir dharmātmā yathā rājā purūravāḥ tathā tvaṃ kuruśārdūla svena dharmeṇa śobhase
english: As the righteous Yayāti shone, as King Purūravas shone, so you, O tiger among the Kurus, shine by your own dharma.

sanskrit: yathā bhagīratho rājā yathā rāmaś ca viśrutaḥ tathā tvaṃ sarvarājabhyo bhrājase raśmivān iva
english: As King Bhagīratha shone, as the celebrated Rāma shone, so you outshine all kings, like the sun with its rays.

sanskrit: yathā manur yathekṣvākur yathā pūrur mahāyaśāḥ yathā vainyo mahātejās tathā tvam api viśrutaḥ
english: As Manu, as Ikṣvāku, as Pūru of great glory, as Vainya of mighty splendor — so are you too renowned.

sanskrit: yathā ca vṛtrahā sarvān sapatnān nirdahat purā tathā śatrukṣayaṃ kṛtvā prajās tvaṃ pālayiṣyasi
english: And as the slayer of Vṛtra once burned away all his foes, so shall you, having destroyed your enemies, protect your subjects.

sanskrit: svadharmavijitām urvīṃ prāpya rājīvalocana khyātiṃ yāsyasi dharmeṇa kārtavīryārjuno yathā
english: Having won the earth through your own dharma, O lotus-eyed one, you shall win renown through righteousness as did Kārtavīrya Arjuna.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam āśvāsya rājānaṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ anujñāpya mahātmānaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus comforted the king, the blessed sage Nārada, taking leave of the great-souled one, vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi dharmātmā tam evārthaṃ vicintayan tīrthayātrāśrayaṃ puṇyam ṛṣīṇāṃ pratyavedayat
english: And the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, reflecting on that very matter, reported to the sages the holy purpose of going on a pilgrimage to the tirthas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhrātṝṇāṃ matam ājñāya nāradasya ca dhīmataḥ pitāmahasamaṃ dhaumyaṃ prāha rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having learned the opinion of his brothers and of the wise Nārada, King Yudhiṣṭhira addressed Dhaumya, who was equal to the Grandfather.

sanskrit: mayā sa puruṣavyāghro jiṣṇuḥ satyaparākramaḥ astrahetor mahābāhur amitātmā vivāsitaḥ
english: That tiger among men, Jiṣṇu, of true valor, the mighty-armed one of immeasurable soul — it is I who have sent him away for the sake of obtaining weapons.

sanskrit: sa hi vīro 'nuraktaś ca samarthaś ca tapodhana kṛtī ca bhṛśam apy astre vāsudeva iva prabhuḥ
english: For he is a hero, devoted and capable, O wealth of austerities, highly skilled in weaponry — a lord like Vāsudeva himself.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hy etāv ubhau brahman kṛṣṇāv arinighātinau abhijānāmi vikrāntau tathā vyāsaḥ pratāpavān triyugau puṇḍarīkākṣau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: For I know these two, O brahmin — both Kṛṣṇas, slayers of foes, the valiant pair; and so does the mighty Vyāsa: three-epoch lords, the lotus-eyed ones, Vāsudeva and Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: nārado 'pi tathā veda so 'py aśaṃsat sadā mama tathāham api jānāmi naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
english: Nārada too knows it thus; he always proclaimed it to me; and I too know them — those two sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: śakto 'yam ity ato matvā mayā saṃpreṣito 'rjunaḥ indrād anavaraḥ śaktaḥ surasūnuḥ surādhipam draṣṭum astrāṇi cādātum indrād iti vivāsitaḥ
english: Thinking 'He is capable,' I have dispatched Arjuna. He is the son of the gods, no less than Indra in power; he was sent away to meet the lord of the gods and receive weapons from Indra.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇāv atirathau kṛpo drauṇiś ca durjayaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putreṇa vṛtā yudhi mahābalāḥ sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve 'strakuśalās tathā
english: Bhīṣma and Droṇa, both atiratha warriors, Kṛpa and the son of Droṇa, the unconquerable — arrayed in battle by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all mighty; all are learned in the Vedas, all heroes, all skilled in arms.

sanskrit: yoddhukāmaś ca pārthena satataṃ yo mahābalaḥ sa ca divyāstravit karṇaḥ sūtaputro mahārathaḥ
english: And he who is ever eager to fight with Pārtha, that greatly powerful one — Karṇa, the son of a charioteer, a great warrior, knower of divine weapons.

sanskrit: so 'śvavegānilabalaḥ śarārcis talanisvanaḥ rajodhūmo 'strasaṃtāpo dhārtarāṣṭrāniloddhataḥ
english: He, swift as a horse and mighty as the wind, whose arrows blaze like fire, whose bowstring sounds like a thunderclap — the dust of battle his smoke, the heat of his weapons like fire, fanned by the wind of the Dhārtarāṣṭra forces.

sanskrit: nisṛṣṭa iva kālena yugāntajvalano yathā mama sainyamayaṃ kakṣaṃ pradhakṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Unleashed as if by Time itself, like the fire at the end of an age, he will burn the tinder of my army — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: taṃ sa kṛṣṇāniloddhūto divyāstrajalado mahān śvetavājibalākābhṛd gāṇḍīvendrāyudhojjvalaḥ
english: But him — that great cloud of divine weapons, fanned by the wind of Kṛṣṇa, bearing its flock of white-horse cranes, blazing with the Gāṇḍīva as its lightning —

sanskrit: satataṃ śaradhārābhiḥ pradīptaṃ karṇapāvakam udīrṇo 'rjunamegho 'yaṃ śamayiṣyati saṃyuge
english: This Arjuna-cloud, surging forward with unceasing streams of arrows, will quench the blazing fire of Karṇa in battle.

sanskrit: sa sākṣād eva sarvāṇi śakrāt parapuraṃjayaḥ divyāny astrāṇi bībhatsus tattvataḥ pratipatsyate
english: That conqueror of enemy cities, Bībhatsu, shall in truth receive directly from Śakra all the divine weapons.

sanskrit: alaṃ sa teṣāṃ sarveṣām iti me dhīyate matiḥ nāsti tv atikriyā tasya raṇe 'rīṇāṃ pratikriyā
english: He alone is equal to all of them — such is my conviction; there is no surpassing him, no counter-action by enemies against his action in battle.

sanskrit: taṃ vayaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ sarve gṛhītāstraṃ dhanaṃjayam draṣṭāro na hi bībhatsur bhāram udyamya sīdati
english: We shall all see that Pāṇḍava, Dhanañjaya, once he has taken up his weapons; for Bībhatsu does not falter when he takes up a burden.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu tam ṛte vīraṃ vane 'smin dvipadāṃ vara avadhānaṃ na gacchāmaḥ kāmyake saha kṛṣṇayā
english: But without that hero, O best among the two-footed, we shall not stay unmindful in this forest of Kāmyaka together with Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: bhavān anyad vanaṃ sādhu bahvannaṃ phalavac chuci ākhyātu ramaṇīyaṃ ca sevitaṃ puṇyakarmabhiḥ
english: Please describe to us another forest, good and delightful, abounding in food and fruit, pure, frequented by those of meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: yatra kaṃ cid vayaṃ kālaṃ vasantaḥ satyavikramam pratīkṣāmo 'rjunaṃ vīraṃ varṣakāmā ivāmbudam
english: There, dwelling for some time, we shall await the hero Arjuna of true valor, as those who long for rain await the rain-cloud.

sanskrit: vividhān āśramān kāṃś cid dvijātibhyaḥ pariśrutān sarāṃsi saritaś caiva ramaṇīyāṃś ca parvatān
english: Describe to us various hermitages heard of among the twice-born, as well as lakes and rivers and delightful mountains —

sanskrit: ācakṣva na hi no brahman rocate tam ṛte 'rjunam vane 'smin kāmyake vāso gacchāmo 'nyāṃ diśaṃ prati
english: Tell us, O brahmin; for without Arjuna we have no liking for this forest of Kāmyaka — we go to another direction.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tān sarvān utsukān dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavān dīnacetasaḥ āśvāsayaṃs tadā dhaumyo bṛhaspatisamo 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Seeing all the Pāṇḍavas anxious and downcast in heart, Dhaumya, equal to Bṛhaspati, then spoke to comfort them.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānumatān puṇyān āśramān bharatarṣabha diśas tīrthāni śailāṃś ca śṛṇu me gadato nṛpa
english: Listen, O bull of the Bhāratas, O king, as I describe the holy hermitages approved by the brahmins, the directions, the tirthas, and the mountains.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ prācīṃ diśaṃ rājan rājarṣigaṇasevitām ramyāṃ te kīrtayiṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhira yathāsmṛti
english: First, O king, O Yudhiṣṭhira, I shall describe to you the eastern direction, lovely and frequented by hosts of royal sages, as I recall it.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ devarṣijuṣṭāyāṃ naimiṣaṃ nāma bhārata yatra tīrthāni devānāṃ supuṇyāni pṛthak pṛthak
english: In that direction, beloved of divine sages, lies what is called Naimiṣa, O Bhārata, where the supremely holy tirthas of the gods are found, each distinct.

sanskrit: yatra sā gomatī puṇyā ramyā devarṣisevitā yajñabhūmiś ca devānāṃ śāmitraṃ ca vivasvataḥ
english: Where flows the holy and lovely Gomatī, frequented by divine sages; where is the sacrificial ground of the gods and the shamitra altar of Vivasvat.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ girivaraḥ puṇyo gayo rājarṣisatkṛtaḥ śivaṃ brahmasaro yatra sevitaṃ tridaśarṣibhiḥ
english: In that direction is the excellent and holy mountain Gaya, honored by royal sages; and the auspicious lake Brahmasaras frequented by the thirty divine sages.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ puruṣavyāghra kīrtayanti purātanāḥ eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yady eko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet
english: On account of which, O tiger among men, the ancients declare: Many sons should be desired, if even one might go to Gaya.

sanskrit: mahānadī ca tatraiva tathā gayaśiro 'nagha yatrāsau kīrtyate viprair akṣayyakaraṇo vaṭaḥ yatra dattaṃ pitṛbhyo 'nnam akṣayyaṃ bhavati prabho
english: There too, O sinless one, is the great river and the Gayashira, where that banyan tree is celebrated by the brahmins as conferring inexhaustible merit, O lord — where food offered to the ancestors becomes inexhaustible.

sanskrit: sā ca puṇyajalā yatra phalgunāmā mahānadī bahumūlaphalā cāpi kauśikī bharatarṣabha viśvāmitro 'bhyagād yatra brāhmaṇatvaṃ tapodhanaḥ
english: There too is the holy-watered Phalguna, a great river; and the Kauśikī, abounding in roots and fruits, O bull of the Bhāratas — where Viśvāmitra, rich in austerities, attained brahminhood.

sanskrit: gaṅgā yatra nadī puṇyā yasyās tīre bhagīrathaḥ ayajat tāta bahubhiḥ kratubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: Where the holy river Gaṅgā flows, on whose banks Bhagīratha, dear one, performed many sacrifices with abundant fees.

sanskrit: pāñcāleṣu ca kauravya kathayanty utpalāvatam viśvāmitro 'yajad yatra śakreṇa saha kauśikaḥ yatrānuvaṃśaṃ bhagavāñ jāmadagnyas tathā jagau
english: And among the Pāñcālas, O Kauravya, they speak of Utpalavata, where Viśvāmitra Kauśika sacrificed together with Śakra; where the venerable son of Jamadagni sang the genealogical hymns.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrasya tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vibhūtim atimānuṣīm kanyakubje 'pibat somam indreṇa saha kauśikaḥ tataḥ kṣatrād apākrāmad brāhmaṇo 'smīti cābravīt
english: Beholding that superhuman glory of Viśvāmitra, Kauśika drank soma at Kānyakubja together with Indra, and then departed from the kshatriya estate, declaring 'I am a brahmin.'

sanskrit: pavitram ṛṣibhir juṣṭaṃ puṇyaṃ pāvanam uttamam gaṅgāyamunayor vīra saṃgamaṃ lokaviśrutam
english: The confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, O hero, holy and sanctified, pure and supremely purifying, beloved of the sages, is famed throughout the worlds.

sanskrit: yatrāyajata bhūtātmā pūrvam eva pitāmahaḥ prayāgam iti vikhyātaṃ tasmād bharatasattama
english: Where the soul of all beings, the Grandfather himself, first performed sacrifice — it is therefore renowned as Prayāga, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: agastyasya ca rājendra tatrāśramavaro mahān hiraṇyabinduḥ kathito girau kālaṃjare nṛpa
english: And there is the great and excellent hermitage of Agastya, O lord of kings — Hiraṇyabindu, as it is called, on Mount Kalanjara, O king.

sanskrit: atyanyān parvatān rājan puṇyo girivaraḥ śivaḥ mahendro nāma kauravya bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Surpassing all other mountains, O king, is the holy and auspicious lord of mountains called Mahendra, O Kauravya — belonging to the great-souled son of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: ayajad yatra kaunteya pūrvam eva pitāmahaḥ yatra bhāgīrathī puṇyā sadasyāsīd yudhiṣṭhira
english: Where the Grandfather himself first performed sacrifice, O son of Kuntī; where the holy Bhāgīrathī was present as a participant, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yatrāsau brahmaśāleti puṇyā khyātā viśāṃ pate dhūtapāpmabhir ākīrṇā puṇyaṃ tasyāś ca darśanam
english: Where that spot is known as the holy Brahmasala, O lord of the people, thronged with those whose sins have been washed away — and meritorious is even the sight of it.

sanskrit: pavitro maṅgalīyaś ca khyāto loke sanātanaḥ kedāraś ca mataṅgasya mahān āśrama uttamaḥ
english: Sacred and auspicious, renowned in the world from ancient times, and also Kedara, and the great and excellent hermitage of Mataṅga —

sanskrit: kuṇḍodaḥ parvato ramyo bahumūlaphalodakaḥ naiṣadhas tṛṣito yatra jalaṃ śarma ca labdhavān
english: Mount Kundoda, lovely, abounding in roots, fruits, and water, where the Naiṣadha king, when thirsty, found water and comfort.

sanskrit: yatra devavanaṃ ramyaṃ tāpasair upaśobhitam bāhudā ca nadī yatra nandā ca girimūrdhani
english: Where lies the lovely divine forest adorned with ascetics, and the river Bāhudā, and the Nandā at the mountain summit —

sanskrit: tīrthāni saritaḥ śailāḥ puṇyāny āyatanāni ca prācyāṃ diśi mahārāja kīrtitāni mayā tava
english: The tirthas, rivers, mountains, and holy sanctuaries in the eastern direction, O great king, have been described by me to you.

sanskrit: tisṛṣv anyāsu puṇyāni dikṣu tīrthāni me śṛṇu saritaḥ parvatāṃś caiva puṇyāny āyatanāni ca
english: Now hear from me the holy tirthas in the other three directions — the rivers and mountains and holy sanctuaries as well.

sanskrit: dhaumya uvāca dakṣiṇasyāṃ tu puṇyāni śṛṇu tīrthāni bhārata vistareṇa yathābuddhi kīrtyamānāni bhārata
english: Dhaumya said: Now hear of the holy tirthas in the southern direction, O Bhārata, described in detail as best as I recall, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yasyām ākhyāyate puṇyā diśi godāvarī nadī bahvārāmā bahujalā tāpasācaritā śubhā
english: In that direction is found the holy river Godāvarī, abounding in gardens, rich in water, frequented by ascetics, auspicious.

sanskrit: veṇṇā bhīmarathī cobhe nadyau pāpabhayāpahe mṛgadvijasamākīrṇe tāpasālayabhūṣite
english: Both the Vena and the Bhīmarathī — two rivers that dispel fear of sin, filled with deer and birds, adorned with the dwellings of ascetics.

sanskrit: rājarṣes tatra ca sarin nṛgasya bharatarṣabha ramyatīrthā bahujalā payoṣṇī dvijasevitā
english: And there the river of the royal sage Nṛga, O bull of the Bhāratas — the Payoṣṇī, with lovely tirthas, rich in water, frequented by twice-born sages.

sanskrit: api cātra mahāyogī mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ anuvaṃṣyāṃ jagau gāthāṃ nṛgasya dharaṇīpateḥ
english: And here the great yogi Mārkaṇḍeya of great austerities sang the genealogical song of Nṛga, the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: nṛgasya yajamānasya pratyakṣam iti naḥ śrutam amādyad indraḥ somena dakṣiṇābhir dvijātayaḥ
english: We have heard that at the sacrifice of Nṛga as the sacrificer, Indra was intoxicated with soma and the twice-born with their sacrificial fees — witnessed directly.

sanskrit: māṭharasya vanaṃ puṇyaṃ bahumūlaphalaṃ śivam yūpaś ca bharataśreṣṭha varuṇasrotase girau
english: The holy and auspicious forest of Mathara, abounding in roots and fruits, and the sacrificial post, O best of the Bhāratas, on the mountain by the stream of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: praveṇyuttarapārśve tu puṇye kaṇvāśrame tathā tāpasānām araṇyāni kīrtitāni yathāśruti
english: And on the northern bank of the Praveni, the holy hermitage of Kanva; and the forests of the ascetics, described as I have heard.

sanskrit: vedī śūrpārake tāta jamadagner mahātmanaḥ ramyā pāṣāṇatīrthā ca puraścandrā ca bhārata
english: The sacred altar at Śūrpāraka, dear one, of the great-souled Jamadagni; and the lovely Pashanatirtha, and Purashchandra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: aśokatīrthaṃ martyeṣu kaunteya bahulāśramam agastyatīrthaṃ pāṇḍyeṣu vāruṇaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: The tirtha of Aśoka among mortals, O son of Kuntī, the hermitage of Bahula; the tirtha of Agastya among the Pāṇḍyas, and the tirtha of Varuṇa, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: kumāryaḥ kathitāḥ puṇyāḥ pāṇḍyeṣv eva nararṣabha tāmraparṇīṃ tu kaunteya kīrtayiṣyāmi tāṃ śṛṇu
english: The Kumaris are said to be holy, among the Pāṇḍyas also, O bull among men. Now I shall describe the Tamraparni, O son of Kuntī — hear of her.

sanskrit: yatra devais tapas taptaṃ mahad icchadbhir āśrame gokarṇam iti vikhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu bhārata
english: Where the gods performed great austerities at the hermitage, seeking the highest — known as Gokarṇa throughout the three worlds, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śītatoyo bahujalaḥ puṇyas tāta śivaś ca saḥ hradaḥ paramaduṣprāpo mānuṣair akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: That lake is cool-watered, rich in water, holy, dear one, and auspicious — supremely difficult of access for men who have not disciplined their souls.

sanskrit: tatraiva tṛṇasomāgneḥ saṃpannaphalamūlavān āśramo 'gastyaśiṣyasya puṇyo devasabhe girau
english: There too, on Mount Devasabha, is the holy hermitage of a disciple of Agastya, the son of Trinasoma and Agni, abounding in ripe fruits and roots.

sanskrit: vaiḍūryaparvatas tatra śrīmān maṇimayaḥ śivaḥ agastyasyāśramaś caiva bahumūlaphalodakaḥ
english: There too is the Vaidūrya Mountain, glorious, made of jewels, auspicious; and the hermitage of Agastya himself, abounding in roots, fruits, and water.

sanskrit: surāṣṭreṣv api vakṣyāmi puṇyāny āyatanāni ca āśramān saritaḥ śailān sarāṃsi ca narādhipa
english: I shall also speak of the holy sanctuaries in Surastra, O lord of men — the hermitages, rivers, mountains, and lakes.

sanskrit: camasonmajjanaṃ viprās tatrāpi kathayanty uta prabhāsaṃ codadhau tīrthaṃ tridaśānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: The brahmins there also speak of the Camasonmajjana; and Prabhāsa, the tirtha of the thirty gods on the ocean, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tatra piṇḍārakaṃ nāma tāpasācaritaṃ śubham ujjayantaś ca śikharī kṣipraṃ siddhikaro mahān
english: There is Piṇḍāraka by name, an auspicious place frequented by ascetics; and Ujjayanta, the great peaked mountain that quickly grants success.

sanskrit: tatra devarṣivaryeṇa nāradenānukīrtitaḥ purāṇaḥ śrūyate ślokas taṃ nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: There an ancient verse celebrated by the foremost of divine sages, Nārada, is heard — listen to it, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: puṇye girau surāṣṭreṣu mṛgapakṣiniṣevite ujjayante sma taptāṅgo nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate
english: 'On the holy mountain among the Surāṣṭras, frequented by deer and birds, Taptanga performed austerities on Ujjayanta and is glorified on the summit of heaven.'

sanskrit: puṇyā dvāravatī tatra yatrāste madhusūdanaḥ sākṣād devaḥ purāṇo 'sau sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Holy is Dvāravatī there, where dwells the Madhusūdana — that one is the primeval God himself, for he is the eternal Dharma.
